title: Kernel affinity and SM saturation probe - Dec 2026
body:
Context:
This is an exploratory capture to understand an intermittent latency spike we see on p2p-enabled clusters when running mixed small/long sequences. The working hypothesis shifted from naive kernel contention to an affinity / scheduling imbalance where small kernels are pinned to the same SMs and long decoder kernels push those SMs into a poor steady state (low warp occupancy, persistent register pressure).

Primary goals:
- Validate whether stream-to-SM affinity heuristics (CUDA stream priorities and persistent kernel placement) create clustered SM saturation.
- Measure per-kernel SM active % and per-SM warp occupancy across a 30s steady-state window.
- Check if host-side enqueue jitter correlates with microbursts of small kernels that collapse occupancy.

Environment & setup:
- HW: A100-SXM4 (8-card testbed, NVLink enabled, p2p on)
- SW: driver 535.x, CUDA 12.2, custom runtime branch sampler/affinity-experiments (branch: affinity-experiments/dec2026)
- Model: decoder-only 6.7B serving workload with mixed-sequence (5% >1024 tokens, 95% <64 tokens)
- Runtime flags: --kv-cache-prefetch=on --continuous-batching=adaptive --stream-priority=enabled
- Capture: Nsight Systems 2026.4 with timeline sampling at 1ms resolution + per-kernel occupancy counters (SM Active %, Active Warps, Avg Active Warps)

Commands used to reproduce capture (notes for ops):
- nv-nsight-cu-cli --target-processes all --metrics sm__thread_inst_executed.avg,sm__warps_active.avg --trace kernel,nvtx --output affinity-dec-08
- run loadgen with seed 42, 1 client thread per GPU, batcher config: max_batch_size 8, max_latency_ms 50

What I looked for in traces (quick checklist):
- long-running decoder kernel durations and overlap with many short attention kernels
- repeated small-kernel bursts within <2ms windows
- localized SMs with high active % and high register spill indicators
- host enqueue gaps >1ms preceding small-kernel bursts

Key observations (raw):
- Observation 1: On 3 captures where we saw the 95th percentile latency spike, the short attention kernels (attention_small_float32_kernel) were clustered in short bursts separated by 0.8–1.6ms idle gaps. Those bursts consistently overlapped with the tail of a persistent decoder kernel on one GPU.
- Observation 2: Per-SM charts show a subset of SMs (SM 2,3,7 on card 0) at ~92% SM active while other SMs were at 48–55%. The imbalance persisted for 20–50ms windows.
- Observation 3: Avg active warps on saturated SMs dropped to ~6.4 (out of 32 logical), indicating lots of serialization despite high SM active %.
- Observation 4: Host enqueue jitter: there are enqueue gaps ~1.2ms preceding bursts, attributable to a short pre-batch scheduling transaction on the host (batcher thread yielding to network callback).
- Observation 5: NVLink p2p transfers interleaved with small kernels; on affected cards we saw increased L2 miss ratios during bursts (indicator: lts__t_sectors_op_read_miss), suggesting memory pipeline contention.

Hypothesis refinement:
- Not a pure kernel-level inefficiency: it's an interaction of (a) stream affinity/pinning that maps small burst kernels onto the same SM subset as the long decoder kernel and (b) host-side enqueue jitter creating microbursts that kick the saturated SMs into lower warp-level parallelism.
- Result: few SMs stay "hot" and see repeated context-like transitions (register pressure + memory stalls) while most SMs are underutilized. Overall GPU utilization looks high but effective parallelism (warp occupancy) is low -> worse latency.

Evidence mapping to counters:
- High sm__inst_executed kernel counts on SM subset + low sm__warps_active.avg -> shows serialization on hot SMs.
- High lts__t_sectors_op_read_miss correlates with small-kernel bursts -> memory-bound microbursts.
- NVTX annotations show batcher->enqueue boundary precisely where host enqueue gaps occur.

Quick experiments & results (what I toggled):
1) Disabled stream-priority and let default round-robin: 95p latency spikes reduced by ~28% in a 10k sample run, but tail still present.
2) Enabled explicit stream-to-SM spread in the runtime (round-robin SM assignment for short kernels via cooperative groups mapping): tail reduced further ~46%, but throughput dropped 2.1%.
3) Artificially injected small random jitter on host dispatch (sleep 50us) to break microburst alignment: tail reduced ~33%, suggests host batching alignment is a strong contributor.

Suggested short-term mitigations (low risk):
- In the batcher: add small randomized offset (10–100us) to dispatch short-kernel streams to avoid synchronized microbursts (config flag: --dispatch-fuzz=on).
- Change default stream mapping heuristic to avoid binding short attention kernels to SMs used by persistent decoder kernels. Add an internal flag: --prefer-spread-for-short-kernels.
- Add telemetry: per-SM warp-occupancy histogram in production traces for 5s windows (help detect hot-SM patterns).

Longer-term ideas (research/engineering):
- Explore a lightweight kernel placement shim that queries current per-SM occupancy (approx) and biases CUDA stream assignment to underutilized SMs. Prototype as a runtime library linked into persistent kernel controller.
- Investigate combining KV-cache prefetch timing with stream dispatch to avoid overlap with host-side NVLink transfers. Stagger prefetches slightly for large sequences.
- Consider kernel fusion for very short attention kernels to reduce number of kernel launches (trade latency for code complexity).

Concrete next steps (action items):
- [Priya] add --dispatch-fuzz flag to batcher, roll to canary cluster (owner: me) by 2026-12-14. (linear: RED-3124)
- [Marcus] instrument per-SM occupancy histogram and ship to console traces (deadline 2026-12-17).
- [Hannah] run 48h soak with stream-priority disabled + dispatch-fuzz enabled and collect 95/99 tail metrics (deadline 2026-12-21).
- [Eng] sync with infra on NVLink telemetry link to see if p2p transfers can be deprioritized during known small-kernel phases.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Does this pattern surface on other GPU types (H100, L40x) with different SM counts / L2 behavior? Need cross-GPU capture.
- Is the small-kernel implementation itself memory-serving inefficiently? A micro-optim of attention_small kernel might remove L2 thrash and resolve issue without scheduling changes.

Notes to self (log):
- Keep affinity-experiments branch short-lived; once we have telemetry to detect pattern, we can try conservative default changes.
- Attach sample Nsight capture to RED-3124 for triage.

Attached artifacts and capture references (local):
- affinity-dec-08.nsight (internal share, see linked_artifacts for Linear/PR cross-ref)
- small-kernel-list.txt (names/params used during capture)

If anyone wants to grab the live capture and walk through with me, ping in #eng-serving-runtime and I can share a screenshare; priority for Marcus/Hannah first since they own telemetry and batcher respectively.

-- Priya
